questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Improving my french, taking courses in french
Spent my gap year in Paris

Additional comments:

questions.answer:
There was a meeting for all Erasmus student the week before school started
The administration was not very helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The administration changed all the exams

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Found accommodation through family friends, lived in their studio in the 9th arr.
If you don't know any, then try the Facebook site Padam madam

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is experience to live in Paris

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have the first two weeks to try out all the courses, then you register at the administration at the end of the first two weeks

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not very helpful, they didn't know a thing

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted but ended up not taking the TD anyway, as they changed the exam form to something more difficult as first promised

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be quick about choosing courses, try as many as possible

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Competent professors

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: What made the courses difficult was them being in French. You don't have to reflect so much and do case studies, mostly just remember by heart

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit boring only having lecturers and writing down notes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Droit international privé
Droit international public
Droit administratif comparé
Droit international pénal
History of codifications
French constitutional law
Duality and other specificities of the french court system

Cours de Français de Spécialité (C1 French Course)

= 37 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Droit international public – easy oral exam, similar to International Law at UCPH
Droit administratif comparé – nice professor, interesting course

Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't join any sports as for example swimming classes were located a bit far away

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to different parts of France: Nice, Bretagne, Normandie

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not that easy to get used to the way of learning

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the French people, don't be shy

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way they had the conference classes, only listening not participating

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Paris is a perfect city to live in when you speak the language

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- don't be stressed about not writing good notes, ask French students or find them on Studocu
- visit as much as the city
- speak French as much as you can

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Administration is very bad

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my french a lot

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having four oral exams in French in 6 days

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Paris is the best city to live in

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
